lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Hello, No. 7.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Looks like you were living it up in your youth, and then got smacked right in the back of the head.
You'd make the same face if you woke up to someone just standing over you.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Is that so?

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Sorry for bothering you first thing in the morning.
What's going on so early?

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Something came up that I need your help with.
Help...?

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: You might not know this, but a new semester is about to kick off at the M.M.R. Vocational School.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: With a bunch of new students coming in, things are bound to get lively.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: For some reason, I've no idea why,

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: the public seems to have a way worse impression of our school than I expected.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: The higher-ups are worried that funding might get cut.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: So this year, we figured we'd try to make the place look a little more normal, like a regular school.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: And that's how

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: the "M.M.R. Vocational School Image Improvement Project" was born.
... And how are you going to pull that off?

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: To improve our image, we're going to hold a festival that the public can take part in.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: But to make that work, we'll need people who can blend in naturally at the school,

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: like you, No. 7.
Wait, so you want me to enroll in the school?

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Exactly.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: I want you to keep the atmosphere at the school relaxed,

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: at least just until the festival's over.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: I've already sent you a file with the details. Look it over when you can.
Am I going alone?

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: No, two others will join you.
Who are they?

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Well...

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: They should be here soon. I sent them the file a little while ago.
Oh...

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: I'm sure this will be quite memorable for you, No. 7.

lines.speaker: ether
lines.text: Have fun at school!
Ether waves lazily and leaves my room.
I go through the file Ether sent me.
It turns out I'll be living in the school dorm for a while.
Guess I should finish up my work here and start packing.
I'm in the middle of everything when...
*Knock, knock*
Someone's at my door.
Come in.
The door whirs as it opens.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Hello, Commander.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Mornin'!
It's Privaty and Arcana,
so that means...
So you two are coming to school with me?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: That's right, I've been hired as a visiting teacher.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Just until the festival, of course.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I'm... supposed to be some kid of library student assistant or something?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Anyway, I'm going in as a student!

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: What about you?
Me?
I guess I'm just... the Commander? OR maybe more like the examiner, like last time?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: You didn't bother to read the file Ether sent, did you?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: It says you're supposed to decide for yourself

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: and prepare whatever role that'll help you fit in naturally.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: You can become a teacher like Privaty, or a student like me.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: It's totally up to you.
Teacher or student... Do we really have to go that far?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Ha, you really don't get it, do you?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: It's all about the immersion!

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: The second I step into the school, I'm no longer part of the Best Seller Squad.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I'll be right in the heart of youth.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Sunlight streaming through the halls, students laughing everywhere...

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: and then, there's you and me...!
Arcana speaks as if she's in a full-blown musical, striking an overly dramatic pose.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Well,

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: she isn't wrong.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: You've worked with me at the school before, so you should know that better than most.
Yeah, I know.
Wow, this is a lot more serious than I thought it would be.
Hearing you say that makes me a little excited, too.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Right? Just thinking about it makes your heart race a little.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: So let's give it our best shot.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I'm not about to let this opportunity slip away.
Arcana holds out her fist.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Well, I'm sure you'll manage just fine, Commander.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: But there's no harm in getting yourself fired up beforehand, is there?
Privaty cautiously extends her fist as well.
I lightly bump my fist against theirs,
careful not to hit too hard.
Living a normal school life...
actually sounds pretty fun.
The days vanish in an instant,
and before I know it, the day before the new semester has arrived.
And I...
make my way into the dorm at the M.M.R. Vocational School, where I'll be staying for the foreseeable future.
Oh wow, this is huge.
It looks like this place is originally meant for four. There are two rooms with bunk beds,
and a spacious living room and kitchen sit in the middle.
It almost feels too big for just one person.
... I guess I should unpack first.
I pull my things out of the suitcase, carefully arranging them.
Clothes, books, and supplies all find their spot.
Finally, I pull out what might be the most important item for this task.
I hold it carefully for a moment, feeling its weight.
It's...
A neatly folded set of spare clothes.
A tablet containing the students' data.
I'm not sure yet...
But if I'm going to be a student, I'll need more than this uniform. Some casual clothes, at least.
I hang the carefully pressed outfits on the hanger,
smoothing out each fold as I go.
I'm not sure yet...
But if I end up as a teacher, it'd be useful to have the students' data on hand.
I carefully place the tablet
where it's most visible on the desk.
Phew... I guess everything's more or less sorted.
It's 7 in the evening.
It's way too early to go to bed, but there's nothing to do while just lounging around...
Maybe I should check out the school a bit.
I don't have time to see the whole campus, so just one area would do.
Where should I go...?
Classroom.
The teachers' office.
The library.
I ponder for a moment, then make my way to the classroom.
I ponder for a moment, then make my way to the teachers' office.
The door slides open with a low rattle.
The teachers' office is dark and empty, a cold draft snaking through the room.
Tomorrow, this place will be filled with students and teachers, and the atmosphere will be completely different.
I take my time looking around, imagining the office alive with chatter and movement.
Among the neat rows of desks, one spot immediately catches my eye.
A desk stacked with boxes that haven't been unpacked yet,
clearly marking this as the desk of a new teacher.
This must be Privaty's desk.
I cast a quick glance over the empty desk and move to step away.
*Clatter*
Something crunches under my foot.
Looking down, I see a cute cat-shaped pen with the exact same color as Privaty's hair.
Looks like it fell out of the box.
I pick up the pen to put it back in the box.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: What are you doing?
Whoa, you scared me!
At the sound of the familiar voice, I turn to see Privaty staring daggers at me.
Privaty, you startled me...

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I should be the one who's surprised.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: What are you doing here alone, with the lights off?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: And...

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: *Ahem* this is my desk.
I was just looking around.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: If you were coming to the teachers' office, you could've at least told me.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I went all the way to the dorm for nothing.
You came to my room? What for?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Th-that's because...!

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I was just making sure you didn't get lost or anything.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: You seem to have made it, so it's fine.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Let's go.
Where to?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: The dorm, obviously.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: You're not actually planning to stay in this gloomy office, are you?
Oh, that's true...
I head back to the dorm with Privaty.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Hmm?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Commander, isn't your room supposed to be on the top floor?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: This is just the second.
I thought I'd walk you back
and see which room yours is while I'm at it.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Wh-what?!

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Why do you need to know that?!
Relax, I'm not trying to do anything... Just thought it'd be good to know.
You already know which room I'm in, anyway.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I-I didn't mean anything by it...!

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I only knew because the school gave out the info on who's staying in the dorms...!

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: So don't go getting the wrong idea!
Relax, I get it.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: ... All right.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Here's my room.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I-if you're going to come by, at least give me a heads-up first.
Will do.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: And you do know there's the new semester speech tomorrow morning, right?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Make sure you're there by 8:00 AM.
Oh right, I nearly forgot about that.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Yes,

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I'll be giving a short speech as the teacher representative.
Wow, really? That's great.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Heh, of course. You can definitely look forward to it.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I've put together the perfect speech.
Privaty puts on a confident front, but I can tell she's slightly nervous.
What should I say...?
It's okay if it's not perfect.
It's not all stiff and formal, right?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: What's that supposed to mean...?
I think you're putting too much pressure on yourself.
I'll be listening too, so just relax and keep it natural.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Wh-what's that supposed to mean?

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: ... You're just making things worse!
Oh... Sorry, my bad.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: It's fine, I see where you're coming from.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I-I'm not sure if it's all just stiff and formal,

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: but I did my best to make it sound proper.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Hopefully, that's not too boring for them...?
They're students, so you don't need to be too formal.
Words from the heart will resonate more than overly polished lines.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: ... That's true.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: They're students, not Nikkes or soldiers.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: And that's exactly what we're trying to focus on this time.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I suppose that makes me feel a little better.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: But!

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Not that it matters, I'd have done just fine anyway.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: Thanks for walking me back, Commander.

lines.speaker: privaty
lines.text: I'll go in now.
All right, get some rest. See you tomorrow.
After saying goodbye to Privaty, I make my way back to my room.
Oh, right!
I pull out the pen I had forgotten about from my pocket.
I should've returned this...
... Oh well.
I place the pen on the desk,
then lie on the unfamiliar bed and try to drift off to sleep.
I ponder for a moment, then make my way to the library.
The quiet hum of the library
is briefly interrupted by the soft scrape of an opening door.
The spring breeze flows in through the open window, carrying the golden light of the evening sunset...
By the window, someone's blue hair flutters gently in the breeze.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Mmm... zzz...
Arcana is fast asleep, completely unaware of what's happening.
What should I do?
Call out to her.
Approach her carefully.
... Arcana.
Her eyelids flutter slightly, then slowly open.
For a moment, she stares at me drowsily.
Then her eyes curve into a smile.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Oh, you're here?
Hey,
what are you doing here?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I've been waiting for you.
Me?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Mm-hmm.
I sit across from Arcana.
Careful not to wake her, I slip quietly over
and sit beside her.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Mmm... zzz...
Arcana sometimes pretends to be asleep just to mess with me,
but now, she really does seem to be asleep.
I watch Arcana in silence.
She must be having a good dream since there's a faint smile on her lips.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Hehe... mmm...

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Huh?!
*Bang!*
Arcana bangs her knee on the desk and bolts upright, but then...
Our eyes meet, and she proceeds to ease back into her seat as if nothing happened.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Y-you're here!
Oh, hey.
Wh-what are you doing here...?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I've been... waiting for you. Mm-hm.
For someone who's supposed to be waiting, you sure slept soundly, huh?
Is your knee okay?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: It really hurts...
Arcana stretches lazily.
How long have you been here?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: *Yaaawn...* Since morning.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Anyway, as part of the library... council? What was it again?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: C-committee? Yeah, that sounds about right.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Since I'm part of the library committee, I figured I'd check out my workplace ahead of time.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: And...
Arcana props her chin on her hand and grins at me.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I knew you'd show up.
... What would you have done if I didn't show up?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Oh, I would've just stayed in the library by myself the whole day and then gone home all lonely.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: ... Wait,

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: that's what I always used to do, isn't it?!

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Still, I trusted that you'd come.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I figured you'd want to check out this place at least once.
Arcana gets up from her seat.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Tomorrow's the big day, huh?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: You all set?
More or less.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Yeah... me too.
Arcana's fingertips trace along the bookshelf.
What do you mean by that?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I've been getting myself mentally prepared.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Physically too, of course, but I'll show you what I mean by that tomorrow.
Arcana smiles and steps closer, taking my hand.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Let's go grab dinner! I haven't eaten a thing since this morning and I'm starving!
Sure, sounds good.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Oh, hold on.
Arcana stops just as she's about to leave the library.
What's wrong?

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I got so caught up in getting ready for school that I totally forgot something.
Arcana steps closer and suddenly hugs me.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: I'm glad you came back safe and sound again.
Arcana lightly taps my chest.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Well...?
... Okay, okay.
I take the Wheel of Fortune card with a note attached out of my pocket.
... I'm back.
A smile spreads across Arcana's lips when she takes the card.

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Yeah...

lines.speaker: arcana
lines.text: Welcome back. I've missed you.
After dinner with Arcana, I head back to the dorm,
and rest up for tomorrow.
